note: Golden wire contract for the sign-in bridge's APP DOOR (DDR 0246, ADR 0236; Ben's rulings on idss #1666 and #1669). matou-app copies THIS file so neither side guesses the wire. Values are illustrative; the fields, paths, statuses and refusal kinds are the contract. Snake_case on the wire.

sign_in_site.rule: ONE string is the sign-in site: the descriptor's signin.url == the ask's door == the address the verifier binds. It is the bridge's own sign-in address.

ask.response_note: This is an ORDINARY service sign-in: it carries NEITHER an offer field NOR credential / cred= (see panel below). It offers no seat unlock, so the wallet shows the plain sign-in card. The negative case is as much of the contract as the positive one.

offer_field.note: WHAT THIS SIGN-IN OFFERS, in a field of its own (ADR 0282's 2026-09-29 amendment, obligation 1a). The wallet reads THIS field, never a sealing key on the code (ek= is retired, 1d), the display name in svc, or cred. Three values, absent being one of them.

values.<absent>: an ordinary service sign-in — it offers no seat unlock; the field is omitted (see ask.response above).
values.seat-unlock: a control-panel sign-in: a seat unlock is on offer, so the wallet shows the sign-in card's unlock line (PU-A2u, on by default).
values.unlock: an unlock hop — a locked panel unlocking through THIS SAME sign-in door (see unlock_hop below): the wallet shows the unlock card (PU-A4) and the bridge dresses the page in its unlock face (PU-S1).

deep_link_params_note: offer= and cred= ride ONLY a control-panel challenge (see panel below): cred= always, offer= = seat-unlock on a control-panel sign-in and = unlock on an unlock hop. An ordinary service sign-in carries the other six and neither. No code carries ek= any more — the sealing key on the code is retired (obligation 1d).

present.url: the ask's present_url, verbatim — never derived from door
present.request_note: The plain (non-panel) present request carries NO armed signal. A control-panel unlock adds armed:true — see panel.present.request below. No sealed_passcode rides any present now (retired, 1d).

no_credential.when: the presented credential is not the one this door asks for (ADR 0289): a committee credential other than administrator at the control panel's door, or ANY committee credential — Administrator included — at a service's door. Verified, then refused: nothing is recorded and no session is earned.

status_poll.verified_note: On verified the poll completes the auth request, sets the 12 h SSO cookie, and hands back the callback redirect. It carries NO handover field — the eager status-poll relay is retired (1d). The steward handover now travels the sign_in_armed_handover routes below.

panel.note: The control-panel sign-in (ADR 0289 + ADR 0282 d.2/d.6 and its 2026-09-29 amendment). The door asks for the ADMINISTRATOR credential and offers a seat unlock; the steward arms with the unlock line on, and on completing the armed sign-in the door mints a single-use HANDOVER CAPABILITY (see handover_capability below) delivered over the OIDC channel. These fields appear ONLY on a control-panel sign-in; an ordinary service sign-in (ask.response, present.request above) carries none of them. No sealing key rides the code and no sealed_passcode rides present — both retired (obligation 1d).

administrator.note: ADR 0289 (Ben, 2026-09-28). The control panel's door ASKS FOR THE ADMINISTRATOR CREDENTIAL and opens on it alone — Membership plays no part, so its holder need not be a community member. Administrator is issued under the COMMITTEE schema, which it shares with every komiti credential, so the schema cannot name it: the ask carries `credential` (and the code `cred=`) = the definition slug, which a committee ACDC carries as its `a.committee` attribute.
administrator.wallet_rule: When the ask carries `credential`, present the held credential whose schema is in `schemas` AND whose `a.committee` equals it — never merely the first credential of an asked schema. When the wallet holds no such credential there is ONE fallback, and only for `credential` = `administrator`: present the held Membership (schema in `schemas`) whose `a.role` is `operator` — the founding operator and any steward still on the legacy role, whom the gateway admits on that Membership until `role` is retired (#1956). A Membership with any other role is NOT presented at this door, and no other credential is ever a fallback. When neither is held, present NOTHING and tell the member: "You do not have the required credential to sign into this service".
administrator.schemas_rule: `schemas` on a panel ask lists the committee schema(s) FIRST, then the membership schema(s). The membership schemas are there for a steward on the legacy role and for a wallet that predates `cred=`; a wallet that reads `cred=` presents the Administrator credential, else a Membership whose `a.role` is `operator`, else nothing — it never presents a `member` Membership or another komiti credential at this door.
administrator.presentation: the Administrator ACDC + its issuance event, as a bare CESR stream — exactly the shape a Membership is presented in
administrator.verified: present → 200 {status: verified}. The session is the administrator's: it opens the control panel, and — for a holder with no Membership — nothing a member's standing opens.
administrator.release_order: The wallet that reads `cred=` is released BEFORE a gateway sends it. A wallet that predates `cred=` presents the first credential it holds of an asked schema, and a panel ask lists the committee schema first — so a wallet holding a komiti credential ahead of its Membership presents that and is refused `no-credential`.

challenge.offer_note: a control-panel sign-in offers a seat unlock (offer_field above). An unlock hop carries offer=unlock instead — see unlock_hop below.

present.request_note: The steward approved with the unlock line ON (PU-A2u at a first sign-in, PU-A4 at an unlock hop), so the wallet ARMS: it sets armed:true and sends NO box on present (it keeps the passcode ready to seal for this one challenge and seals only when the freshly-landed panel asks, sign_in_armed_handover below). On completing an armed control-panel sign-in the door mints a single-use HANDOVER CAPABILITY (see handover_capability) — never derived from the AID — and delivers it to the panel over the OIDC channel (userinfo), NOT this wallet→door wire. The panel presents that capability, not the forgeable AID cookie (#1966), to the door's bind/collect to ask for the box. An unlock hop is a control-panel hop, so an armed unlock mints the capability by the very same rule; an unarmed present completes as a plain sign-in and mints nothing.
present.no_sealed_passcode: No sealed_passcode rides present any more (retired, 1d). The eager option-A relay — the wallet sealing at Approve to a key that rode the code, the door relaying the ciphertext on the status poll — is gone from the wire; the live path is sign_in_armed_handover below.

handover_capability.note: The panel-handover capability (idss #1967). On completing an ARMED control-panel sign-in — a first sign-in or an unlock hop — the door mints a high-entropy, single-use token — 256 bits of crypto/rand, base64url, NEVER derived from the AID — bound to that one sign-in's challenge and dying with it. It is delivered to the panel over the OIDC channel, NOT this wallet→door wire: it rides the USERINFO endpoint ALONE (the `handover_capability` claim), never the id token (which tends to be persisted/logged). The gate that holds the token captures it and a panel-readable route exposes it; the panel presents it to bind/collect (#1961). The wallet neither reads nor carries it — it is here so the copy on both sides records where the capability lives.

unlock_hop.note: A LOCKED panel unlocks through THIS SAME SIGN-IN DOOR (ADR 0282's 2026-09-29 amendment, obligations 1a–1d). There is ONE unlock mechanism, not two: the panel's own unlock code (matou://unlock, /login/app/unlock/*) is RETIRED and answers 404. Instead, a locked panel sends the browser to the gate's sign-in start carrying prompt=login; the gate carries that to the bridge, which ALWAYS ASKS (never completes silently from the session the steward already holds), dresses the page in its unlock face (PU-S1), and mints the code that says offer=unlock. The ask is unchanged — the Administrator credential (ADR 0289), the same as any control-panel sign-in.

gate_marker.carrier: prompt=login (standard OIDC force-reauthentication) — the implementer's carrier under ADR 0174. The gate forwards it to the bridge's authorize; prompt=none is refused at authorize as before.
gate_marker.rd_rule: rd is validated same-apex exactly as today (an open redirect is a phishing door).

unlock_hop.present: same as panel.present above — an armed unlock present mints the handover capability, an unarmed one completes as a sign-in and mints none.
unlock_hop.page: the bridge renders the sign-in page in its UNLOCK FACE (PU-S1): the unlock heading in place of the welcome line, a still-signed-in note (it must never read as signed out, d.3), the way back to the control panel, and NO twelve-words link. The words unlock lives on the panel (PU-M0).

sign_in_armed_handover.note: The SIGN-IN-ARMED steward handover (ADR 0282 d.2/d.6 + its armed-consent amendment, ruled Ben 2026-09-28; idss #1961). The panel loads signed in but LOCKED, mints a fresh Ed25519 Signer in tab memory, and asks the door for the box belonging to the sign-in it just completed — one tap, no second scan, NO secret in any URL or history entry. It proves it may ask with the single-use HANDOVER CAPABILITY its armed sign-in minted (handover_capability above, #1967), delivered over the OIDC channel and read back over the community session (GET /api/v1/panel/handover) — NEVER the forgeable AID cookie (#1966), never a URL. The armed wallet (matou-app#674) reads the panel's verkey and seals to it. Three routes below; matou-app copies them so neither side guesses the wire. A box on a sign-in that armed NOTHING (no capability minted) is refused, as today.

panel_bind_collect.who: the control panel (admin.<apex>), cross-origin to the door (id.<apex>)
panel_bind_collect.request_note: The capability (delivered over the OIDC channel, #1967) and the tab's Ed25519 verkey qb64 ride the BODY — NEVER a query string, so no secret is in any URL, fragment or history entry. The panel sends the SAME verkey on every poll: the first call binds it, later calls poll for the box. A later call carrying a DIFFERENT verkey is a hijack attempt and is refused (already-bound).

waiting.note: bound; the armed wallet has not sealed yet. Keep polling.

answered.note: the sealed box (ciphertext only) + the AID the door recorded as signed in, handed to the tab EXACTLY ONCE then deleted. `handover` is a CESR qb64 X25519_Cipher_Salt cipher the door cannot open. `aid` is what the opened agent MUST match (ADR 0282 d.6).

unknown_capability.note: a forged token, or a public AID passed off as a capability — it authenticates nothing; the AID is an input nowhere in this path

already_bound.note: a bind with a DIFFERENT verkey after one is bound — a hijack attempt

spent.note: the box was already collected — the capability is single-use; a second tab gets nothing and stays locked (AC 3)

expired.note: the sign-in's two-minute challenge has died — the arm dies with it (AC 4)

wallet_key.who: the wallet, keyed by the challenge it armed (held from the scan)
wallet_key.answered_note: the verkey the panel bound (a PUBLIC key). Empty ({}) until the panel has bound one, or on an unknown/dead challenge — the wallet polls for a second or two after Approve, then gives up (the panel lands on PU-M0x cause 1).

wallet_seal.who: the wallet, posting the box sealed to the panel's verkey
wallet_seal.request_note: the door keeps only the CIPHERTEXT — never plaintext — and relays it to the panel's collect once. `sealed_passcode` is a CESR qb64 X25519_Cipher_Salt cipher.

not_armed.note: a box for a sign-in that armed NOTHING (no capability minted) — refused (AC 7)

no_key.note: the panel has not bound a verkey yet — nothing to seal to (a stale/racing post; the wallet reads the key first)

spent.note: a box was already posted or collected — single-use
